messages:
Maria: FYI support got a ticket from ACME — p99 latency jumped to ~2.8s around 09:10 UTC, multiple users. They say it correlates with a traffic spike. Can eng-platform take a look?
Kevin: looking. Any customer request IDs or sample traces?
Maria: sample trace ids: trace=acme-9f3a, acme-9f3b. Repro steps: send 20 concurrent requests with prompt size ~800 tokens. They saw queueing / 'admit' messages in logs.
deploy-bot: deploy completed "service/ingress-gw v2.14.1" at 2026-03-17T09:05:10Z by ci/cd-pipeline (sha: a1b2c3)
Sato: pulling metrics now — ichart shows admission_controller_queue_length spiking from 10 -> 250 at 09:06-09:12. Also per-tenant concurrency for tenant=acme hit 120 which is our configured soft limit.
Kevin: hmm, did the deploy change admission thresholds? I don't see threshold changes in PR. Could be traffic pattern + new request fanout behavior.
Jen: oncall: we can temporarily raise tenant concurrency cap for acme and enable burst pool, that should reduce tail. Want me to do that?
Maria: please do, customers are complaining. Also include fallback to model-small variant if latency persists.
Sato: running command to bump tenant concurrency:
```
# admin-cli
admin-cli tenants update --id acme --max-concurrency 250 --burst-enabled true
```
Sato: done. Queue length dropped from 250 -> 40 within 45s, p95 improved from 1.1s -> 0.45s, p99 from 2.8s -> 0.9s (metrics: ingress.histograms).
Kevin: good short-term. We still need a root cause: why did acme hit the soft cap? logs show a sudden increase in short-lived parallel requests due to their client retry behavior + a newer fanout feature that expands sub-requests.
Maria: ACME confirms they rolled a client change yesterday to parallelize prompt slicing. They didn't throttle.
Sato: opened an issue to add per-tenant burst tokens + backpressure shaping to avoid priority inversion (link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ingress/issues/487). Proposed fixes: 1) per-tenant queue weight, 2) graceful degradation to small model, 3) admission-controller fix to prefer fair-share instead of FIFO.
Kevin: action items: (a) eng-runtime to implement fair-share scheduler (Sato), (b) platform to add temporary auto-bump rules for enterprise tenants with burst pools (Kevin), (c) support to get ACME to roll client throttling (Maria).
Maria: I emailed ACME with mitigation steps and asked them to throttle to 50 concurrent. They acknowledged.
Jen: will keep monitoring and revert the bump after traffic normalizes. Also adding a postmortem note to incidents channel. :thumbsup:
Sato: quick log snippet from admission controller at spike time:
```
[09:07:04] admit: tenant=acme current=118 max=120 inflight=202 queued=128
[09:07:04] admit: decision=queue reason=concurrency_exceeded
[09:07:05] worker-dispatch: dropped=3 due_to=timeout
```
Kevin: thanks. I'll schedule a small follow-up to scope ETA for the fair-share scheduler. Good catch everyone.
Maria: closing the ticket for now pending ACME client change and runtime fix. Will reopen if regressions recur.
